Another restaurant we went to in Philly was Zahav, which has been on our radar for years— @jimmarzo even has the cookbook. 🫓 @all_xk kindly secured the hard-to-get reservations well in advance for us. 🫓 We were a table of 5, which was good as all the courses are meant to shared. After the starter called “In the Beginning,” the menu is divided into 4 parts from which each diner chooses a dish.🫓 The “In the Beginning” course started off super strong with a large assortment of small dishes accompanied by homemade laffa bread that was honestly to-die-for. I especially loved the beets and pickled Napa cabbage. But already this course was a ton of food. 🫓 Next up was the mezze course (which I forgot to photograph). Since we were 5 people, we tried 5 of the 6 options. My favorite was the phyllo-wrapped haloumi. To be honest, after the huge (and already satisfying) starter, this additional course of more small plates seemed unnecessary. 🫓 After that, was the al Ha’esh course with assorted shashlik (skewers), which we bypassed because we were saving room for our mains (mesibah). 🫓 The rest of the table was excited for the pomegranate lamb shoulder, for which Zahav is well-known, and I had the grilled black bass. Unfortunately, the others said the lamb was dry and not very flavorful as there was too little pomegranate sauce which stuck to the bottom of the pan (However, the Persian rice that accompanied it was a hit). My fish was cooked well but again, lacking in any discernible flavor. 🫓 From there —already stuffed to the max—we moved on to dessert, which we enjoyed as there were several sweet-tooths at the table. 🫓 In the US, portions are notoriously large, but in this case, we each left the restaurant with enough take-away food for a few days. Personally, I could have dined on the first course alone (with a few extra pieces of that awesome bread) and ended with a dessert, and the meal would have been perfect. 🫓

Set inside a historic 19th-century townhouse just steps from Broad Street, Vetri has been serving refined #Italian cuisine since 1998—when #MarcVetri transformed Philly’s dining scene with his intimate 32-seat jewel box of a restaurant.

🍴 The journey:

• #FoieGras Pastrami – a legendary signature, silky richness cut by spice and smoke. One of my favorite bites of the evening!
• #BeefHeartTartare – bold yet elegant.
• Bluefin #TunaCarpaccio – delicate, ocean-bright freshness.
• #SmokedSpaghetti with Clams, Corn & Scallions – rustic seaside flavors elevated with a kiss of smoke.
• #Pappardelle with #Rabbit & Peaches – a rustic-meets-playful balance.
• Classic split: pillowy Spinach #Gnocchi + ethereal Almond #Tortellini with #Truffle.
• #Branzino – cooked to perfection with tomatoes, olives, and a potato galette.
• #VealMilanese – golden and perfectly crisp, a true #Milanese classic.
• #MoltenPistachioCake with #MintStracciatella #IceCream – the finale you dream about.
• A touch of old-world hospitality: #PetitFours to close the evening.

📍 #Philly icon. Timeless flavors. A meal that lingers long after the last bite and remains a cornerstone of Philadelphia’s fine dining history.

@alpenrosephl 

One of the hardest reservations in Philly… and it starts with the entrance.
The door is so hidden it feels like a steakhouse speakeasy —
no sign, no lighting, just a mysterious façade you’d walk past without noticing.

Step inside and the whole atmosphere shifts:
dark wood, candlelit tables, vintage lamps, and a room that feels straight out of a 1920s film.

Highlights:
• Smoked Old Fashioned — table-side, aromatic, unforgettable
• Dry-aged steak with deep, clean flavor
• Bone Marrow Toast that’s rich but beautifully balanced
• Onion ring tower that’s shockingly crisp and light
• Flaming dessert that steals the show 🔥

Alpen Rose is perfect for anniversaries, birthdays, or a night you want to truly impress someone.
It’s not just dinner — it’s a full experience.

@butcherandsinger 

If Alpen Rose is dramatic and cinematic,
Butcher and Singer is timeless, classic, and effortlessly elegant.

No smoke, no theatrics — just perfectly executed steakhouse dishes in an old-school New York setting.
Leather booths, warm lighting, impeccable hospitality… it’s consistent every single time.

Ideal for:
• Company dinners
• Business meetings
• Family gatherings
• Anyone who appreciates classic steakhouse perfection

It’s the kind of place you can return to again and again and always walk out satisfied.

Final take:

✨ Alpen Rose — for the “wow” moment, special occasions, and unforgettable experiences.
✨ Butcher and Singer — for reliability, comfort, and true classic steakhouse charm.

Two styles. Two moods. Both worth the trip.

Tom Lubbe of Matassa Roussillon, nestled between the Pyrenees and the Mediterranean, is commonly known for easy table wine—but producers like Matassa are redefining the region with one-of-a-kind, delicious wines that highlight its true potential. thier old vines are incredibly low-yielding, resulting in intense concentration and focus

currently in the shop:

'Cuvée Marguerite' 2023: a blend of Macabeu, Muscat d'Alexandrie, and Muscat Petit Grain and named after Tom's wife Natalie's grandmother. whole cluster, co-fermented in concrete, and spends up to a month on the skins. the wine is then aged for 8 months on the lees in foudres. notes of tropical fruits and flowers, rich and refreshing on the palate

'Cuvée Romanissa' 2023: a single vineyard wine named for it's soil composure of iron-rich red schist, Romanissa is 100% Grenache, known as Lledoner Pelut in Catalonian dialect. aromatic on the nose, red fruits and flowers, and herbs are paired with silky tannins
